candidate: routed-expert prefill takes a registered grouped-prefill family when the weight's quant key declares one: one launch per (expert, out_col) reads that expert's weight row once and reuses it across the expert's rows, instead of one launch per (out_col, lane) re-reading the whole expert weight matrix once per lane (hipengine/kernels/hip_gfx1100/gemma4/gemma4_experts.py)
reason: the incumbent prefill re-reads every expert's weights once per lane, and on this artifact the two expert projections are 84.8% of the 512-token prefill kernel time. Reusing each expert's weights across its own rows removes that re-read, and for Q5_1 it is free: the grouped kernel's column walk and strict 256-wide reduction tree are the same association as the selected GEMV's, so the route is bit-exact and consumes no numerical budget. Where a quant registers no grouped family the projection keeps the per-lane GEMV unchanged, so the change is a cost decision the quant key already declares rather than a model-level switch.

attribution.method: rocprofv3 --kernel-trace over one 512-token prefill on the strict tree (scripts/gemma4_campaign_bench.py --prompt 512 --output 1 --samples 1 --warmup 0), kernel time summed by kernel name
attribution.reading: the two expert projections are 84.8% of prefill kernel time and are the only prefill cost that scales with (lanes x weight bytes) rather than with weight bytes

mechanism.route: gemma4_project_experts_rows() tries, in order: the grouped family when the block has at least one compact row per expert and the quant key registers one, then the per-row selected GEMV, then the per-expert offset path. The route that ran is recorded in gemma4_moe_expert_route_counts().
mechanism.bit_exactness: both kernels accumulate a row as `column = t, t + 256, ...` over 256 logical threads and reduce with the same strict 256-wide binary tree, so the grouped route is bit-identical to the selected GEMV rather than merely close
mechanism.artifact_mix: the UD-Q4_K_XL file is not one quant: 29 of 30 layers are (gate/up Q4_K, down Q5_1) and layer 29 is (gate/up Q5_K, down Q8_0). Only the Q5_1 down projection has a registered grouped family with this ABI, so 29 of the 60 expert projections per prefill block move to the grouped route and the other 31 keep the per-lane GEMV.

correctness.bit_exactness_test: tests/test_unit_gemma4_expert_route.py asserts bit-identical bf16 outputs between the grouped route and the selected GEMV at (out, in) = (2816, 704), (1408, 2816), (64, 128), (37, 96) and (16, 32); (2816, 704) is the artifact's own down-projection geometry and 704 is not a multiple of the 256-wide reduction
correctness.kernel_test: the same file checks the grouped kernel against a dequantized Q5_1 reference with an empty expert in the middle of the expert list, so a kernel that shifted rows after an empty expert or ignored the compact row order fails
correctness.intended_path: confirmed on the public surface, not inferred from timings: hipengine.LLM.generate_detailed() on a 413-token prompt reports gemma4_moe_expert_route_counts() == {"selected_gemv": 151, "grouped_prefill": 29}. That is exactly the expected split for one prefill block plus two decode steps: 29 grouped = the Q5_1 down of the 29 Q4_K/Q5_1 layers, and 151 per-lane = 30 gate/up + 1 Q8_0 down for the prefill block plus 30 x 2 x 2 for the two decode steps.
